conclusion: Merged request/chunk metadata reuse is not a gfx1151 128K lifecycle fix. A cached exact 512/1 preflight completed, but the bounded 128K warmup produced no completed timing and entered the same persistent 100%-activity, 2.9-GHz, low-power state. The last retired chunk marker certifies all work through token 61440; host execution enters layer 18 linear attention in chunk [61440,65536) and never reaches layer 19. Unlike the pre-merge capture, current main prepares chunk metadata before the layer loop, so layer 18 was entered. Chunk granularity still cannot name the last retired user dispatch or distinguish a nonterminating kernel from queue/fence no-progress. The failure moved from measured prefill 1 near 32K in the pre-merge capture to the first warmup near 64K here, arguing against one deterministic chunk/layer location and remaining consistent with timing-sensitive KFD/MES/queue lifecycle failure.
